title: A study's tables, as samples by features and samples by variables
summary: Turns a microbiome study into the two tables every tertiary tool takes: samples by features at one rank, and samples by variables carrying every column the study knows. A shape change only — nothing is filtered and no cohort is chosen, so what to compare stays open and is named downstream.

third_party.name: pandas
third_party.note: Supplies the pivot and the join. Nothing here decides a number.

environment.provenance: No image. Runs in the statistics domain's virtual environment, which is where pandas is pinned for this tree.

activation.note: Entered by putting its bin directory first on PATH.

determinism.note: A pivot and a join. Nothing is sampled and row order does not reach the output, which is sorted by sample.

resources.memory_hint: The long table is read whole before it is pivoted, so memory follows the source table rather than the result.

inputs.name: abundances
inputs.description: The study's long per-sample abundance table, one row per sample per feature.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The study's sample table, one row per sample.

inputs.name: subjects
inputs.description: The study's subject table. Joined on so subject-level variables can be used as cohorts too.

outputs.name: features
outputs.description: Samples by features, sample_id in the first column. Unfiltered. What it feeds is declared here rather than in each general engine, because correlation and diversity run on any table and an entry in statistics naming a science would point the dependency backwards. Charting is deliberately not listed: almost every table is chartable, including results of the capabilities below, so a planner inferring it would be choosing between several right answers rather than deriving one.

outputs.name: metadata
outputs.description: Samples by variables, sample_id in the first column, carrying every sample-level and subject-level column the study holds.

outputs.name: assembled
outputs.description: What was built and what can now be grouped by: every metadata column, and the values of the ones with few enough to list.

parameters.name: omic
parameters.description: Which of the study's long tables to pivot: metagenomics or metabolomics.

parameters.name: rank
parameters.description: For an omic whose table carries several levels, the one to build features at: species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom. Ignored where the omic has no levels.

interpretation: Nothing is filtered here. Every tool downstream applies its own prevalence and abundance rule, so a feature absent from a result was dropped by that tool and not by this one. Choosing what to compare is not part of this: name a column of the metadata as the grouping when calling the tool. A grouping that is not already a column is built in run_code as one column keyed by sample_id and joined to this metadata, rather than by rebuilding these tables.
